authenticity.why_registration_is_not_blocked: The missing thing is the donor's weights. A registration does not read them: it fixes, before any run, what will be extracted, how many operations each extraction may spend, what schema the output has, what threshold counts as the headline, and which failure modes will be reported. Every one of those is decidable now. Deferring the registration until the weights arrive would be the R2 failure this repository has already paid for once: a run whose thresholds were chosen after the shape of the data was known.

calibration_findings_recorded_after_the_.why_this_block_is_here_and_not_inside_th: R2 forbids a registration choosing its thresholds after seeing data. The budget stayed 24, the threshold stayed 10x, the schema stayed v1: none of the pre-run numbers moved.

donor_matrices_touched: the k x 768 gram of the already-read neighbour rows
1_embedding_geometry_into_candidate_feat.implemented_as: cosine similarity of the probe's row of wte against all of wte, top-k neighbours, then a single-linkage cluster over those neighbours to propose a candidate pool. Reads wte once.
1_embedding_geometry_into_candidate_feat.operation_note: one similarity search against wte, plus one gram over the k neighbour rows. The gram multiplies a matrix ASSEMBLED from donor rows, so it is counted; the mutual-nearest-neighbour linking that follows touches no donor matrix and is not.
1_embedding_geometry_into_candidate_feat.plan_words: nearest-neighbour structure of the token-embedding matrix, clustered into candidate feature pools
1_embedding_geometry_into_candidate_feat.what_it_would_mean_on_real_weights: a pool of donor-adjacent tokens, which MP-E12b would compile through grow_pool.

donor_matrices_touched: wte as the tied unembedding (768 x 50257)
2_association_edges_from_unembedding_and.implemented_as: the probe embedding, rescaled by the final layer norm, multiplied by the unembedding to score every vocabulary row, top-k taken as associative successors; plus a read of each registered head's value slice applied to the probe, whose output directions are the values that head writes. NO autoregressive loop, NO sampling, NO generated text.
2_association_edges_from_unembedding_and.plan_words: for probed tokens, top-k associative successors read from the unembedding and head structure in single matrix operations, not generation
2_association_edges_from_unembedding_and.registered_head_subset: 4 heads, fixed by (layer, head) index in the probe configuration and named in every artifact. The subset is registered BEFORE any figure exists; selecting heads after seeing results would be the selection-after-shape failure R2 names.
2_association_edges_from_unembedding_and.weight_tying_consequence: GPT-2 ties the unembedding to the token embedding, so extraction 2 and extraction 1 read the SAME matrix. They are not two independent measurements of the donor and the artifact must not present them as such. See pre_registered_failure_modes.2.

3_circuit_motifs_heads_as_directed_maps_.implemented_as: for each registered head, its output projection slice applied to the probe gives the direction that head writes when it attends to the probe -- a directed association map, recorded as source, target, direction and confidence. For each layer, the probe is multiplied by the MLP input projection and the top-responding neurons are the features the donor associates with it; their output rows are the values those features write. A neuron's response is a read, not a run: no forward pass is executed.
3_circuit_motifs_heads_as_directed_maps_.plan_words: attention heads read as directed association maps, and MLP neurons read as key-value feature detectors - the top-responding neurons for a probe are the features the donor associates with it
3_circuit_motifs_heads_as_directed_maps_.why_12_layers_are_all_read: the plan's claim is about the donor's library, not about a subset of it. Reading a subset of layers would be a registered limitation; reading all twelve costs 12 operations and removes the caveat.

extractions_registered.counting_rule_for_a_matrix_operation: ONE matrix operation = one multiply of a probe vector by one donor parameter matrix, of any shape, plus one similarity search against one donor matrix. Element-wise arithmetic (layer-norm rescale, gating masks, top-k selection) is NOT counted, because it touches no donor matrix and its cost is linear in one dimension rather than in the vocabulary. The rule is registered so that the budget is checkable by a reader rather than by the tool that spent it.

gate: G5 (opens now as a PARALLEL track; it does not open G4, G5 or G6 and it does not close G2)

hard_per_item_read_budget.arithmetic: extraction 1 = 2 (one search against wte, one gram over the neighbour rows it returned), extraction 2 = 5 (one tied-unembedding read, one W_V read per registered head), extraction 3 = 16 (one W_O read per registered head, one c_fc read per layer, twelve layers). Total 23 spent by design against a budget of 24: headroom 1. The number is not a margin picked after the fact; it is the design's cost plus one, and the unit test that pins the per-item count at 23 is what stops the plus-one from quietly becoming a plus-six.
hard_per_item_read_budget.arithmetic_corrected_before_any_run: the first draft of this file counted extraction 1 as 1 operation. The implementation's neighbour gram made it 2. Corrected before any measurement existed, and recorded here because a budget whose arithmetic was fixed after a run would be a budget chosen to pass.
hard_per_item_read_budget.enforcement: C3 of the plan's own C-conditions: 'read budget exceeded on any logged item - abort the extraction'. The counter is in the extraction path, not in a report: an item whose count would exceed 24 raises and writes nothing.
hard_per_item_read_budget.logged_and_sealed: every item's actual operation count is written into the artifact, per extraction and per probe, so a reader can audit the budget against the counting rule rather than against the tool's summary.
hard_per_item_read_budget.unit: matrix operations per probed association, as defined by the counting rule above

harness_hashes.note: Hashes are checkout-stable by construction. See seal_basis and the module docstring for the measurement behind it. reseal_history records every superseded value.

registrations_excluded.why: registrations are ledgers, not evidence. Two registrations that seal each other form a cycle no stamp sequence can satisfy, so cross-registration entries are dropped and the fact is recorded here rather than left as a DRIFT that never clears.

also_recorded: sha256_lf (equal to sha256_of_git_blob, proven per file)
seal_basis.chosen: (a) seal the git blob, not the worktree bytes
seal_basis.rejected: (b) a .gitattributes pinning eol -- it changes line-ending behaviour repository-wide, which is a policy decision, not a gate artifact
seal_basis.verification: tools/registration_seal.py --check recomputes both and asserts they agree
seal_basis.why: core.autocrlf=true with no .gitattributes means worktree bytes != blob bytes, so a worktree-byte seal cannot verify after commit+clone. Verified on the tracked 1.4 MB evidence file: worktree 1,473,837 CRLF bytes, blob 1,421,862 LF bytes, and `git hash-object` returns the index blob, so the conversion is applied.

self_excluded.why: a file listing its own hash is stale the moment the hash is written; --check can never be clean otherwise. Its content is still pinned transitively by the artifacts that cite it, and by git history.

stamp_ordering.note: git_dirty_sealed is the field to act on. A non-empty list means at least one file this seal hashes is not yet in the commit it names -- the seal is anchored to a commit that cannot reproduce it. Stamping a second registration right after the first is NOT that case, because registrations are excluded from every seal.
procedure: 2. run registration_seal.py <registration.json>   # git_head now contains those blobs
4. registration_seal.py <registration.json> --check   # must be clean at that HEAD
stamp_ordering.rule: COMMIT FIRST, THEN STAMP, THEN COMMIT THE STAMP. Never stamp while a file this seal hashes is uncommitted -- that is what git_dirty_sealed reports, not mere tree dirt.
stamp_ordering.why: git_head is the commit the seal claims to describe. If the sealed bytes are still uncommitted when the stamp is taken, git_head names a commit that does not contain them, and there is no checkout you can verify the seal against.

open_decisions.D-MPE12-05: RULED 2026-08-10 by PI -- see pi_rulings['D-MPE12-05']. H2's claim is UNDER-SPECIFIED and that is the finding: the read-versus-inference ratio must be reported as a CURVE against generated-token count (minimum 1, 5, 9 and the donor's measured mean answer length), with the verdict stated at each point, and the claim registered as conditional on that definition. Choosing the length after seeing which lengths pass is the R2 event refused here in advance.
open_decisions.D-MPE12-05_as_registered_before_the_ruli: How many generated tokens an 'equivalent association query' is, for H2. THE BINDING ONE, and it was not visible from the plan text: the synthetic calibration measured that the pre-registered 10x threshold is crossed at 5 generated tokens on operation count and at 9 on MACs, and is NOT reached on wall-clock at any registered length (a factor of 5.8 at nine tokens, and under 2.0 at one). The plan says 'at least ten times cheaper per association than inference' and never fixes the association's length, so the verdict is a property of an unstated definition rather than of weight-reading. Raised by the measurement, not by reading ahead -- see experiments/MP-E12/results/probes_synthetic_calibration.json calibration_findings.1.

D-MPE12-05.if_only_the_longer_framings_pass: the claim must be RE-WORDED to name its own condition rather than presented as a property of weight-reading. On the synthetic calibration the shorter framings do not pass (2.13x at one token on operations, 0.70x on wall-clock), so this branch is the likely one and the re-wording is pre-authorised rather than improvised.
D-MPE12-05.implementation_note: The curve shape is already in the sealed artifact's benchmark_vs_reference_inference list; what changes is that a single number may never be lifted out of it.
D-MPE12-05.ruling: MP-E12c must report the read-versus-inference ratio as a CURVE against generated-token count, never as a single number, and must state the verdict at each point on the curve. The curve carries at minimum 1, 5 and 9 generated tokens -- the three points at which this registration's own calibration crossed or failed to cross 10x -- plus the donor's MEASURED mean answer length, which cannot be known until the real donor is present and is therefore registered here as a required point rather than a value.
D-MPE12-05.status: RULED. The ruling is that the claim is UNDER-SPECIFIED, and that this is the finding -- not a gap to be filled with whichever choice reads well.
D-MPE12-05.the_R2_event_this_forecloses: Choosing the association length after seeing which lengths pass would be the R2 event this project has refused repeatedly, and it is refused here in advance: the points on the curve are fixed by this ruling, before the real donor exists, and no point may be added, dropped or headlined selectively.
D-MPE12-05.the_plan_sentence_and_its_condition: The plan's 'at least ten times cheaper per association than inference' cannot be evaluated until an association's token length is fixed. H2 is therefore registered as CONDITIONAL on that definition: the condition is part of the claim, not a caveat under it.
D-MPE12-05.what_the_ruling_does_NOT_do: It does not make the 10x threshold measurable about GPT-2 -- the calibration that produced these ratios ran on a synthetic donor and its quoting guard forbids quoting any of it as evidence about GPT-2. What it settles is the FORM of the eventual figure, which is a decision the PI can make without the weights.

plan_text_transcribed_verbatim.appendix_A_2_read_budget_and_benchmark: A.2 The Read Budget and the Benchmark. Every extraction in MP-E12a carries a per-item read budget: a maximum number of matrix operations per probed association, fixed in the registration file, with every item's operation count logged and sealed. The benchmark compares, on identical hardware and an identical association query set: static reading (the budgeted extraction) against autoregressive inference (the donor generating the association token by token). Reported quantities: wall-clock, operation count, and energy estimate. The pre-registered threshold for H2 is that reading is at least ten times cheaper per association than inference.
checklist_B_6: 1. MP-E12a (opens when G0-prime closes; parallel to G1-G2): implement the three read-only extractions against the GPT-2 124M weights with per-item read budgets; log and seal operation counts.
2. Emit the typed association graph (nodes, edges, confidences) to a versioned schema.
3. Benchmark reads against autoregressive inference on the same hardware and query set; the 10x threshold is pre-registered.
4. MP-E12b: implement the compiler - grow_pool from clusters, grow_plastic and wire_pool from edges, confidence-gated; add the provenance tag and the coverage-gate source dimension, sealed per edge.
5. Run the text-distillation control: the donor emits text once, offline; Droso trains on it through the normal curriculum.
6. MP-E12c: run H1-H3 - transfer versus text-distillation at equal exposure; the latency comparison; retention and refusal suites post-transplant, word-level graded.
7. Emit before-and-after paraphrase and acquisition figures; write decision.md.
plan_text_transcribed_verbatim.section_6_5_MP-E12: Objective. Establish a knowledge-transfer channel that no published system has: teach the connectome to read a trained network's weights statically, without running it, and re-express what it reads in its own currency. Unchanged from v1.0; this is the flag-plant. Concept. A trained network's weights are a compressed association library, paid for at training time. The only interface the industry uses for that library is inference: run the model token by token, and pay latency and energy on every query. MP-E12 replaces the interface. The connectome reads the weight matrices directly - a bounded number of matrix operations per probed association, no autoregressive loop, no sampling - compiles the associations into pools and plastic synapses, and then discards the donor. The library is read once and owned; nothing of the foreign network remains resident. This is why the delays disappear: reading is not running. Stage MP-E12a - weight-reading probes. Read-only; touches only the donor, and is therefore parallelizable from the moment G0-prime closes under rule R4. Donor: GPT-2 124M public weights - deliberately the same model family already used as the program's reference opponent. Three extractions, each a static pass. First, embedding geometry: nearest-neighbour structure of the token-embedding matrix, clustered into candidate feature pools. Second, association edges: for probed tokens, top-k associative successors read from the unembedding and head structure in single matrix operations, not generation. Third, circuit motifs: attention heads read as directed association maps, and MLP neurons read as key-value feature detectors - the top-responding neurons for a probe are the features the donor associates with it. Deliverable: a typed association graph (nodes, edges, confidences) produced under a hard per-item read budget, logged, sealed, and benchmarked.
plan_text_transcribed_verbatim.section_6_5_MP-E12b_and_c: Stage MP-E12b - the weight-to-connectome compiler. Compile the association graph through the existing primitives: grow_pool for discovered feature clusters; grow_plastic and wire_pool for association edges, gated by confidence. Every transplanted edge carries a provenance tag - source model, extraction method, confidence - compiled in the same discipline the repository already applies to measurement rows (git, interpreter, live-state). The coverage gate gains a source dimension: curriculum-learned and library-read knowledge become distinct classes, which is what protects refusal. Stage MP-E12c - verification, three falsifiable hypotheses. H1 (transfer): Droso bootstrapped from the library beats Droso trained on text alone - at equal corpus exposure - on paraphrase probes and on acquisition of new material. The binding control is the text-distillation arm: run the frozen donor once, offline, to emit text, and feed that text to Droso through its normal curriculum. Weight-reading must beat or match text-distillation at lower latency and energy; if it does not, the weights carried nothing beyond their own outputs, and that null result is itself the first controlled measurement of its kind. H2 (latency): per-association read cost is at least ten times lower than autoregressive inference for equivalent association queries, on identical hardware (matrix-operation count, wall-clock, energy). H3 (honesty preserved): retention stays at the invariant, the refusal suites are unchanged after transplantation, and the agent can refuse to ground library-sourced claims - the source dimension works. All three are graded under R9 at word level. C-conditions and gate G5. C1: any guarded row answered post-transplant - abort. C2: library-sourced knowledge silently promoted to curriculum class - abort. C3: read budget exceeded on any logged item - abort the extraction. Full go only if H1, H2 and H3 all hold: paper 3 headline. Partial go: the compiler ships as diagnostic tooling and the transfer result is reported exactly as measured. Null: a negative-results paper - the flag is still planted, because a controlled null on weight-reading into a non-backprop substrate does not exist yet. What MP-E12 is not. It never runs the donor for answers, never fine-tunes the donor, never wraps a transformer around Droso, and never leaves donor weights resident at deployment. Rule R1 holds: the library is read through native compilation, and the connectome remains the only thing that thinks. Known risk. Representational superposition: donor features share dimensions, so extracted edges can be noisy. Mitigations: breadth of the probe battery, confidence gating at compile time, and the text-distillation control that bounds expectations in advance.

1_representational_superposition.how_it_will_be_seen: a probe whose top-k neighbours and top-k successors disagree sharply, or whose neuron responses are dominated by a few high-variance directions, is superposition, not a wrong answer. The artifact reports the disagreement per probe rather than averaging it away.
1_representational_superposition.mitigations_registered_by_the_plan: breadth of the probe battery, confidence gating at compile time, and the text-distillation control that bounds expectations in advance.
1_representational_superposition.plan_words: Representational superposition: donor features share dimensions, so extracted edges can be noisy.
1_representational_superposition.what_would_make_this_stage_fail_honestly: a graph whose edges are so noisy that no confidence threshold separates them. That is a result, and the plan's null branch already provides for it.

2_tied_weights_make_two_extractions_one_.consequence_registered: any figure that combines them must say the donor is weight-tied, and the graph's provenance field carries the matrix name so the tie is visible per edge.
2_tied_weights_make_two_extractions_one_.statement: GPT-2 ties wte and the unembedding, so extraction 1 (nearest neighbours in the embedding) and extraction 2 (top successors from the unembedding) read the same matrix. An agreement between them is partly arithmetic, not two independent confirmations.
2_tied_weights_make_two_extractions_one_.why_this_is_registered_before_the_run: on random weights the tie is invisible in the numbers; it becomes a live interpretation error only when real associations are read. Registering it now is the whole point of a pre-registration.

3_read_budget_exhaustion_on_a_logged_ite.consequence_registered: the artifact records aborted items and their would-be cost, and the operation total is reported with the count of items that were refused, so a budget-limited graph cannot be read as a complete one.
3_read_budget_exhaustion_on_a_logged_ite.statement: an item that would spend more than 24 operations aborts the extraction (C3). The failure mode is a silent truncation: a graph that looks complete but is missing its most expensive probes.

probe_configuration.probe_items_synthetic: the 24 token ids 0..23 of the synthetic donor's vocabulary, one probed association each, so the operation budget is exercised on a fixed and reproducible item count

quoting_guard.meaning: No figure in any MP-E12a artifact may be quoted as evidence about GPT-2, about the ten-times claim, or about the flagship result. The donor is synthetic; there is no library in it.
quoting_guard.no_stage_b_work_has_been_done: Confirmed on 2026-08-10: stage a's calibration is the only MP-E12 run that exists, and no synthetic figure from it has been quoted as evidence about GPT-2 in any document in this repository.
quoting_guard.open_decisions_at_generation.snapshot_is: This list records what was open when the guard was WRITTEN (before any run), and D-MPE12-05 has since been RULED on 2026-08-10 -- see pi_rulings['D-MPE12-05'] and open_decisions['D-MPE12-05']. The list is kept as a dated snapshot per R5, not corrected.
quoting_guard.rule_source: This registration, and the plan's own What MP-E12 is not. Established practice in this repository: MP-E10's sweep and G2's H4 clause both attach a guard naming what the artifact is and is not evidence of.
quoting_guard.still_blocking_a_scored_run_after_this_r: the donor itself, which is a physical absence, not a decision. Nothing in the open list above prevents the code path from being built and tested; the absence prevents it from being pointed at anything real.

status: REGISTERED BEFORE ANY RUN, per rule R2. No donor has been read. The weights are not on this machine.

synthetic_donor.how_it_is_made: tools/mp_e12_synthetic_donor.py, deterministic from a registered seed (1249), float32, standard normal scaled by 0.02 the way a GPT-2 checkpoint is initialised. The donor's own shape manifest is sealed so that a later reader can check that the stand-in had the shape the budget was sized against.
synthetic_donor.named_synthetic_in_every_field: every artifact this stage writes carries donor_is_synthetic: true, donor.name: 'synthetic-124M-shaped-random', and a quoting guard naming the donor. No field of a synthetic artifact may be lifted into a sentence about GPT-2.
synthetic_donor.what_it_can_prove: that the three extractions run, that they read only the matrices the registration names, that the operation counts match the counting rule and fit the budget of 24, that the schema validates, that the abort path fires on an over-budget item, and that the read-versus-infer operation comparison holds at these shapes.
synthetic_donor.what_it_cannot_prove: anything about GPT-2's associations, pools, motifs, confidences or the ten-times claim in the world. Random matrices have no library to read. A number from this donor that appears in a sentence about the flagship result is a reporting error, and this file is the place that would have been violated.
synthetic_donor.what_it_is: A randomly initialised tensor set with the SAME SHAPES as GPT-2 124M: wte (50257 x 768), wpe (1024 x 768 -- n_positions is 1024; a 1500-row wpe would be 356,736 parameters wrong and would not be the donor), and for each of 12 layers c_attn (768 x 2304) split into 12 heads of d_head 64, attn c_proj (768 x 768), mlp c_fc (768 x 3072), mlp c_proj (3072 x 768), plus the layer-norm vectors and ln_f. The unembedding is tied to wte, as in the real model. Total parameters 124,439,808, COMPUTED from the config by the generator and checked against GPT-2 small's published count rather than typed in from a model card.
synthetic_donor.why_a_stand_in_and_not_a_wait: the same discipline MP-E10 used. Its hash-projected token vectors were labelled a stand-in, and the calibration they made possible found three properties of the sealed organ that 23 unit tests had missed. A shape-correct donor makes the extraction path executable and testable now, so that when the weights arrive MP-E12a is a download rather than a build.
